author: Copilot
body: `shiftPressed = shiftPressed || WindowsFunctions.IsShiftState()` will treat *any* currently-held Shift as “navigate backwards”, including Shift that was already down to type an uppercase letter. This appears to contradict the keyboard hook’s existing behavior of only tracking Shift after the toolbar is visible (to avoid uppercase conflicts), and can cause Space navigation to unexpectedly go backwards when the user triggers Quick Accent while holding Shift for capitalization. Consider tracking the Shift state at toolbar-show time (and only applying the async-key fallback if Shift transitioned after the toolbar became visible), or moving the fallback into the hook where you can distinguish “Shift used for uppercase” vs “Shift used for navigation” reliably.

author: Copilot
body: The hard-coded off-screen move to (-10000, -10000) may still land on-screen for large multi-monitor layouts (e.g., several 4K monitors positioned to the left/top can extend beyond -10000 in virtual screen coordinates), which would reintroduce the flicker this is trying to avoid. Consider computing a guaranteed-offscreen position using the virtual screen bounds (e.g., via GetSystemMetrics(SM_XVIRTUALSCREEN/SM_CXVIRTUALSCREEN/SM_YVIRTUALSCREEN/SM_CYVIRTUALSCREEN)) and placing the window just outside that rectangle.

author: daverayment
body: Good call. Updated the code to render offscreen 1000 pixels top-left of 0,0 in virtual screen space, in commit [59261e0](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/pull/46593/commits/59261e0dedfbe0a7d6288268d9add0d736f38d6c)

author: daverayment
body: This was an excellent catch. I've implemented the suggested logic in commit [59261e0](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/pull/46593/commits/59261e0dedfbe0a7d6288268d9add0d736f38d6c). The new code tracks the initial state of the shift key when the popup is summoned, i.e. the user is typing a capital letter, and checks against this when determining the subsequent shift state in `ProcessNextChar`, disregarding the current hardware shift state if the initial state was true, i.e. only relying on the keyboard hook in that case. This means we still get the better async shift state handling for lowercase letters and we don't accidentally move backwards when the user is typing a capital letter.

author: Copilot
body:
`ScrollViewer.HorizontalScrollBarVisibility="Auto"` combined with `IsHitTestVisible="False"` and `Focusable="False"` can show a horizontal scrollbar that the user cannot interact with (mouse/keyboard). If the intent is programmatic scrolling only (via `ScrollIntoView`), consider hiding/disabled the scrollbar instead, or re-enabling hit-testing/focus so the scrollbar is functional.
```suggestion
            ScrollViewer.HorizontalScrollBarVisibility="Hidden"
```

author: Copilot
body: When `_selectedIndex` is `-1` (the common initial state), `characterName.Text` is left unchanged, so the UI can display the XAML placeholder text or a stale description from the previous invocation. Consider explicitly clearing the text (or collapsing the description area) when there is no valid selection, e.g. on show when `_selectedIndex < 0` and/or in the `else` hide path.

author: Copilot
body: Bumping `Microsoft.Windows.CsWin32` in `Directory.Packages.props` affects every project in the repo that consumes CsWin32 and increases the blast radius of this QuickAccent UI fix. If this version change is not strictly required for the new APIs used here, consider reverting the global bump (or isolating it to a separate PR) to keep this change atomic and reduce risk of unrelated build/interop diffs.

author: Copilot
body: The off-screen pre-position uses a fixed 1000px offset from the virtual screen origin. If the selector window ends up wider/taller than 1000px, part of it can still appear on-screen (and flicker) before the final SetWindowPosition runs. Consider computing an off-screen point based on the full virtual screen bounds (e.g., subtract SM_CXVIRTUALSCREEN/SM_CYVIRTUALSCREEN or window size + margin) to guarantee the window is completely outside the virtual desktop.

body: Not addressed: `ScrollViewer.HorizontalScrollBarVisibility="Auto"` is intentional per the PR author's explicit feedback (see [comment](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/pull/46593#issuecomment-3043424143)). The scrollbar provides visual feedback when there are more characters than fit on screen. Since the ListBox is navigated programmatically via `ScrollIntoView`, the scrollbar serves as a passive visual indicator — this is by design, not a bug.
